note: Code derivation: item IS the source column name (BLOCKS regex melt by name, no positional step). The deposit has NO item text at any level -- one .xlsx, no variable/value labels, no cell comments, no second sheet -- and the figshare record has no linked paper, no references and no related materials; OpenAlex and web search found no Milson (2026) article. Text is therefore the canonical RSES (text_source=canonical_instrument), transcribed from the UMD sheet JPEG with its '**' reverse markers stripped as the page instructs ('Do not print the asterisks'). ORDER DECISION: two RSES orders circulate and the rights holder's own sheet uses the LESS common one (1 person of worth, 2 good qualities, 3 failure, 4 as well as most, 5 not much to be proud of, 6 positive attitude, 7 satisfied, 8 more respect, 9 useless, 10 no good; negatives 3,5,8,9,10). The data reject that order and support the commonly circulated one (1 satisfied, 2 no good, 3 good qualities, 4 as well as most, 5 not proud, 6 useless, 7 person of worth, 8 more respect, 9 failure, 10 positive attitude; negatives 2,5,6,8,9): polarity-class split ranks 2nd of 126 partitions (0.048) vs 106th (-0.015) for the UMD order; 'good qualities' is the highest-mean item at position 3 (2.83; next 2.53) whereas the UMD order would put it at position 2 (1.82, 2nd lowest); position 8 has the scale's weakest item-rest r (0.283 vs 0.54-0.78), the known behaviour of 'I wish I could have more respect for myself'. Order within each polarity class beyond positions 3 and 8 is NOT established -- the best split {2,6,8,9,10} beats the claimed one by 0.010, i.e. 5 and 10 are not cleanly separated. RESP DIRECTION: all 45 inter-item correlations are positive (0.12-0.64) and SE_Total equals the raw row sum in 904/904 rows, so the five negatively worded items are stored ALREADY REVERSED; direction higher = higher self-esteem is fixed by 'good qualities' at 74% on 3-4 and 'more respect' at 90% on 1-2 (majority AGREE, as that item usually draws). Anchors therefore run Strongly Disagree(1)..Strongly Agree(4) for items 1,3,4,7,10 and Strongly Agree(1)..Strongly Disagree(4) for 2,5,6,8,9. Anchor spelling from the UMD page prose ('Strongly Agree=3, Agree=2, Disagree=1, and Strongly Disagree=0'); the sheet header prints them in capitals. The UMD sheet's own numbering (1=STRONGLY AGREE..4=STRONGLY DISAGREE) is NOT the stored coding and was not used. Instructions left blank: the canonical UMD instruction ('...IF YOU STRONGLY AGREE, CIRCLE SA...') is a paper-form instruction, and what this (likely online) survey displayed is unknown. Administration language assumed English (UK university, English-language deposit); no language column.
public_note: Item text is the canonical English Rosenberg Self-Esteem Scale; the study's deposit carries no item wording or labels, so the assignment of Rosenburg_esteem_1..10 to items follows the commonly circulated RSES numbering (not the different order printed on the University of Maryland sheet), which the data support by keying structure and marker items but do not pin item-by-item. Responses are stored already reverse-scored (higher = higher self-esteem), so the anchors shown for items 2, 5, 6, 8 and 9 run from Strongly Agree (1) to Strongly Disagree (4).
